item.title: Canada–India Security Pact Risks Enabling Transnational Repression: Sikh Federation Canada Letter to Public Safety Minister
item.dc:creator: Sikh Siyasat Bureau
item.description:
In a formal submission to Minister Gary Anandasangaree, Sikh Federation Canada has voiced deep concern over Ottawa’s decision to deepen security and intelligence-sharing mechanisms with New Delhi. Warning that bilateral counter-terror and extradition frameworks could be weaponized against Sikh dissidents, the advocacy body demanded an immediate suspension of these arrangements alongside an independent public inquiry into Indian transnational repression on Canadian soil.

item.title: India Continues to Weaponize Terrorism Laws to Detain Religious Minorities: USCIRF Cites Jagtar Singh Johal, Umar Khalid’s Case
item.dc:creator: Sikh Siyasat Bureau
item.category: The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF)
The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF)
item.description:
The United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) is sounding the alarm over India's continued use of the UAPA anti-terror law to target and detain religious minorities. While welcoming the recent bail of British-Sikh activist Jagtar Singh Johal, the USCIRF is urging the U.S. State Department to advocate for other detained activists like Umar Khalid and has renewed its recommendation to designate India as a Country of Particular Concern (CPC).
